evidence.exact_quote: PM exposes a single direct-provider grouping named `Free Models` for supported active free/free-limited upstream entries, while preserving the underlying provider, model, account/profile, auth surface, billing/entitlement, transport, quota, and source identity. The wrapper must not rewrite canonical stored provider/model ids into `free_models/*`; it must retain `provider_entry_id`, `provider_family_id`, `model_provider_id`, canonical provider/model ids, stable PM imported ids, hidden subprovider/auth/quota metadata, source refs, and alias/rename/provider-move mappings. Catalog presence or freshness does not prove `usable_now`, quota health, routing readiness, capability support, or policy eligibility.

items.impact: Preserves native provider identity and prevents catalog presence from being misrepresented as runtime readiness.
items.statement: Free Models is a direct-provider presentation wrapper over supported entries, not a new canonical provider namespace or proof of route readiness.
items.title: Free Models preserves provider and route identity

evidence.exact_quote: Free Models Auto Apply tracks the configured upstream source/channel for `vava-nessa/free-coding-models`, imports trusted catalog/settings/runtime-behavior material through PM-owned schemas, and applies validated Free Models changes automatically on checks. PM checks on app launch plus daily background by default, with configurable cadence, but launch checks run after startup in the background and keep last known-good active until validation completes. Runtime behavior changes are automatic only for the Free Models provider and must enter PM through PM-owned declarative router, probe, normalizer, fallback, source-resolver, test, activation, quarantine, and rollback records.

items.impact: Constrains automatic upstream adaptation to validated, PM-owned records while keeping startup nonblocking and last-known-good active.
items.statement: Auto Apply performs background launch and daily checks, validates trusted Free Models material, and activates through PM-owned quarantine and rollback boundaries.
items.title: Auto Apply is Free-Models-scoped and last-known-good

evidence.exact_quote: The Free Models priority setting is a PM-wide top-10 provider/model list across all providers and models. The default setup stays global and paid-first: paid providers/models are preferred over Free Models unless the user ranks Free Models above them. Section, surface, and role-specific PM model settings override the global top-10 and must disclose requested/effective behavior. Outside-top-10 fallback is deterministic by eligibility, policy, setup, cost, pressure, provider availability, and saved user ordering; it must not use recommendation, quality-rank, coding-strength, online-review, local-learning, or benchmark/probe-calibration language in this version.

items.impact: Maintains user order, paid-first defaults, scoped override authority, and requested/effective disclosure.
items.statement: The global top-10 spans all providers, scoped settings override it, and outside-list fallback is deterministic without recommendation semantics.
items.title: Global top-10 precedence and fallback boundary

segments.summary: Reviewed catalog identity, Auto Apply lifecycle, global top-10 precedence, first-run sequencing, and availability/setup behavior. Exact contracts are strong, but Auto Apply atomicity, fallback total ordering, and Multiple issues dominance remain underspecified.

Reviewed provider-native metadata policy, capability epoch, replay matrix, and effort settlement. High-risk gaps remain in unknown-route fail-closed behavior, untrusted metadata lifecycle, and settlement correlation/idempotency.

Reviewed capability epochs, model routing, confidence UI, entitlement/quota settlement, and provider policy. Publication ordering, router reproducibility, settlement remediation/redaction, and policy precedence require normative closure.

Reviewed replay and error contracts, capability authority retirement, residual schema closure, and evidence-bound Usage UI. Remaining seams concern replay-policy ownership, partial-stream recovery, epoch replacement concurrency, and Usage display precedence/privacy/accessibility.
